extracted.intended_audience: poets and spoken-word performers looking to enter or organize a poetry slam
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for finding, signing up for, understanding rules of, and (if needed) hosting a spoken-word poetry slam so a poet can take a poem from page to stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have poem written and performance rehearsed
rubrics_metrics.description: Your poem has been written and your performance has been rehearsed: Now it's time to enter a poetry slam!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare yourself for a successful poetry slam entry by using these tips. (Page also links to additional 'tips for writing and performing slam poetry' and 'slam poetry examples' for inspiration and advice.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Find a poetry slam (where to look)
rubrics_metrics.description: There isn't one centralized group in the U.S. that organizes all poetry slams, so finding one near you may take a little creativity and perseverance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search local bulletin boards (coffee shops), local newspaper event sections, online event listings specific to your area; research venues that regularly hold open mic nights (coffee shops, bookstores, performing arts centers) because some evenings may be dedicated to poetry slams. Consult Poetry Slam, Inc.'s online listings, Youth Speaks for youth opportunities, and the site's comprehensive database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure out the sign-up method (varies by event)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signing up may be as simple as putting your name on a sign-up sheet a few minutes before the poetry slam starts, or it could be as competitive as auditioning beforehand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because sign-up procedures vary with the size and demand of the slam, contact the organizer before you prepare your poem and go to confirm the required sign-up process (walk-up sign-up, pre-registration, or auditions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn and follow the slam rules to keep competition fair
rubrics_metrics.description: Even though there are few rules when it comes to writing slam poetry, a poetry slam usually sticks to strict rules to keep the competition fair.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical rules include: a time limit of around three minutes per performer; no props, costumes, or music may accompany the poem; judging is done by chosen members of the audience on a 0–10 scale. Note that audience behavior (snapping, cheering) is often encouraged and can influence scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand judging: audience-selected judges and 0–10 scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging by chosen members of the audience is based on a scale of 0-10 and can be influenced by a rowdy audience that is typically encouraged to snap and cheer to show approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect subjective scoring tied to performance and crowd reaction; plan delivery and crowd engagement accordingly since audience energy can impact numeric scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host your own poetry slam when none exist locally
rubrics_metrics.description: If you can't find a poetry slam in your neighborhood, you can host your own—invite a small group to your home or school, or rent a performance space for a few hours and charge an entry fee from performers to recoup expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing, structure the event by consulting National Poetry Slam rules for guidelines on how to run a slam. Consider venue, audience, sign-up process, potential costs, and whether to charge performers an entry fee to cover expenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use external resources for inspiration and structural guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The page points to additional resources for creating and performing slam poetry as well as examples submitted by other poets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need help writing or performing, review linked 'tips for writing and performing slam poetry' and published 'slam poetry examples.' For event-structure rules, reference National Poetry Slam rules and listings on Poetry Slam, Inc. and Youth Speaks.
